chunks: From him, from ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥakam, from Sayf ibn ʿUmayrah, from ʿAbd al-Aʿlā, who said:
I asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the supererogatory prayers of the day,

He said: Sixteen rakʿahs, whenever you have the energy. Indeed, ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام had hours in the day in which he would perform salat; when an estate or the ruler occupied him, he would make them up. The supererogatory prayer is only like a gift: whenever it is brought, it is accepted.

key_terms.النَّهَارِ: the daytime period in which these nawafil are performed
key_terms.الْهَدِيَّةِ: a gift, used here as a likeness for the voluntary prayer
key_terms.سِتَّ عَشْرَةَ: the number sixteen, indicating the total rakʿahs mentioned
key_terms.قَضَاهَا: he made them up after missing their usual time
key_terms.نَافِلَةِ: supererogatory prayer performed in addition to the obligatory salat
key_terms.نَشِطْتَ: when you are energetic or feel able

ai.seo_question: What is the time and ruling for the daytime nawafil in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that the nawafil of the day are sixteen rakʿahs and indicates flexibility in their timing when one is ready and able. It also cites the practice of Imam ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn عليه السلام, who would make them up if worldly duties or authority prevented him, emphasizing the accepted nature of supererogatory worship.
